summary: Multnomah County, OR lookout cabin built on Mount Talapus in 1933 and since removed; 1934 panoramas survive; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says the cabin has since been removed; firelookout.com describes it as abandoned; no removal date is given

events.note: Lookout cabin built on the site (register and firelookout.com); firelookout.com lists it as abandoned, with no date given for that
Panorama photos taken June 25, 1934; Forest Lookouts credits Robert Cooper, and the register copy is courtesy of Tammy McLeod
Registered October 14, 2019 as US 1767, OR 508; nominated by Tammy McLeod

evidence.supports: a lookout cabin was built on the site in 1933 and has since been removed
evidence.quote: A lookout cabin was built on the site in 1933 and has since been removed.

evidence.supports: the site is on the Mount Hood National Forest in Multnomah County, Oregon
the U.S. Forest Service administers the site
panorama dated 6-25-1934, courtesy of Tammy McLeod
evidence.quote: Mount Talapus panoramic 6-25-1934 - courtesy of Tammy McLeod

evidence.supports: the cabin is listed as built 1933 and abandoned
about 18 miles north-northwest of Mount Hood
panorama photos taken June 25, 1934, credited to Robert Cooper
evidence.quote: June 25, 1934: Panorama photos taken by Robert Cooper.

evidence.supports: the Forest Service project of 1933 to 1935 aimed to collect panoramas from every fire lookout in Oregon and Washington
evidence.quote: Between 1933 and 1935, the Forest Service in Oregon and Washington undertook an ambitious project to collect high quality panoramic photos from every fire lookout in the region.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts credits the June 25, 1934 panorama to Robert Cooper as the photographer. The register shows a panorama of the same date as courtesy of Tammy McLeod, which names the supplier rather than the photographer. The two credits do not conflict.

notes_for_editor: Only four pages were read and none describes staffing, fires, the removal date or the site today. The link between the 1934 panorama and the 1933 to 1935 Forest Service survey is inferred from the dates, not stated by any source. Access is not recorded.
